claims.text: A 5-10% volume fraction of coherent L12 precipitates can be formed within an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The proposed L12 precipitates can have Al3Ti or Al3Ni chemistry.
Coherent L12 precipitates will restore significant orbital magnetic moments.
Coherent L12 precipitates will pin magnetic domain walls.
Introducing the precipitates will increase coercivity above 100 Oe.
A single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix with Ti in solid solution has suppressed orbital moments.
The single-phase control will have coercivity below 10 Oe.
Annealing between 600°C and 800°C can induce coherent L12 precipitation while preserving a continuous fcc matrix.
Magnetic ordering in the proposed alloy will be maintained from 300 K to 600 K.
Coherent L12 precipitates induce local lattice distortion that enhances spin-orbit coupling.
Interfaces between the fcc matrix and ordered precipitates break local electronic symmetry.
Interface-induced symmetry breaking restores the orbital moment suppressed in the single-phase solid solution.
The precipitates act as barriers to domain-wall motion and increase the energy required for magnetization reversal.
The dual-phase alloy will retain high saturation magnetization while achieving magnetic ordering above room temperature.
Annealing a single-phase Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy at 1000°C produces a homogeneous fcc solid solution with coercivity below 10 Oe.
Loss of precipitate coherency or formation of Laves or Heusler phases could degrade mechanical properties, disrupt magnetic coupling, or cause microcracking.
Ti stabilizes the L12 phase in the proposed fcc-based system.
Related Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti alloys can contain coherent L12 precipitates in an fcc matrix together with an additional Heusler-type phase.
The hypothesis is falsified if coherent L12 precipitates are confirmed but the dual-phase batch has coercivity below 100 Oe.
The hypothesis is also falsified if the dual-phase batch shows no orbital-moment difference from the single-phase control or loses magnetic ordering below 300 K.

contradictions.description: The alloy is defined as Fe-Co-Ni-Ti with no Al addition, yet the proposed precipitates are Al3Ti or Al3Ni. Forming either named phase requires an Al source that is absent from the stated composition and intervention.
The operating regime is described as significantly above room temperature, but the stated range begins at 300 K, which is approximately room temperature.
